summary: Retained for retrospective model-development research under an isolated-rows protocol that is STATED AS A REQUIREMENT, not enforced by the shipped runner: the illustrative runner contract passes the whole eval feature table to the predictor. This version closes the v2026.10 cross-row outcome channel by construction: the independent 2026-11-01 audit recovered 196/372 eval and 286/884 holdout labels exactly from eight shipped outcome-derived history columns (cumulative-count x rounded-rate arithmetic and subtraction), and none of those columns ships in v2026.12 - the frame is issuance attributes plus issue-date recency only (11 columns), with the label source columns absent from every shipped file as the gate asserts. The register is revised in place and publishes no historical vintages, so training-label timing and full-row historical availability are unverified; the vintage is the pinned 2026-06-16 snapshot and the task is declared retrospective, never a point-in-time reconstruction. Measured finding carried beside every figure: the stock runner baseline (eval AUC 0.5068) trails the register-side site-persistence reference (0.6124) by 0.1056 on identical eval rows (the v2026.10 diagnostic on the same rows measured the analogous deficit with paired intervals excluding zero) - no demonstrated headroom under this protocol; the comparison, not the top-line AUC, is the release's scientific content.
supported_uses: Retrospective research and method comparison on the pinned 2026-06-16 vintage under an enforced isolated-rows protocol (one row predicted without any other row)
Agent evaluation under the same enforced protocol, with the labeled eval split as development/validation data and the holdout kept outside agent development until a design is frozen
Study of advisory-duration regime shift (the measured 2020-2022 spike) and of prevalence drift under a temporal split
unsupported_uses: Operational or real-time forecasting claims: no historical-vintage availability evidence exists and none is claimed
Point-in-time historical reconstruction: the publisher revises in place; a future re-fetch measures churn, not past knowability
Any evaluation that gives the predictor whole-table access to eval or holdout features without acknowledging that isolated rows is the declared protocol and enforcing it
Quoting the model AUC (0.5068) without the persistence comparison (0.6124, observed gap 0.1056) beside it

NO adversarial pass beyond the gate and the smoke probe has run on the new bytes - the fresh pre-flip audit must re-run the frozen subtraction attacks and hunt beyond them, and must rule on the frozen quality.json's inherited known_event declaration (see limitations) before any flip

limitations: Single pinned vintage (register content current as of 2026-06-16); the publisher updates quarterly and revises in place, so no historical operational-availability claim is possible

The isolated-rows requirement is design intent, not runtime enforcement: the shipped illustrative runner passes the whole eval feature table to the predictor, and an evaluator that wants the declared protocol must enforce it

No demonstrated headroom: the stock baseline trails the site-persistence reference by 0.1056 on identical rows; the task's discriminative claim above simple references is not established by the runner's own baseline

No per-row diagnostic ran on this frame: no model Brier, no per-issue-year model figures, and no recomputed model-vs-persistence interval exist for v2026.12; the interval figures quoted in the docs belong to the superseded v2026.10 frame on the same eval rows and are labelled as such

The frozen quality.json carries the builder's v2026.10-era known_event declaration naming two register rows and their durations, including one scored holdout row; for this internal-threshold task the gate requires no such fixture and does not verify that block, so it is inherited voluntary content inside accepted bytes - the pre-flip audit must rule on it, and a fixture-to-train-row fix would change the artifact version (a new reviewed release)

Prevalence shift inside eval (0.7442 in 2018 to 0.4153 in 2020) and the 2020-2022 duration-regime spike inside holdout make pooled figures unrepresentative; per-issue-year tables are mandatory reading

Site identity is register free text with variants (no clean entity key); history features use a stated normalisation rule and 19 same-(site, issue date) pairs + 1 triple exist (16 pairs with two valid durations - label noise, counted)
The holdout was never evaluated; no holdout figure exists and its first use must follow a frozen design
